items.head: Traffic Separation Scheme
items.quote: A Traffic Separation Scheme (Delaware Bay) has been established off the entrance to Delaware Bay.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage on Delaware Bay, Delaware River and tributaries thereof is compulsory for all foreign vessels of 100 gross tons or more and all U.S. vessels under register engaged in the foreign trade or commerce of 100 gross tons or more. Pilotage is optional for all U.S. Government vessels and for all U.S. vessels in the coastwise trade that have on board a pilot licensed by the Federal Government for these waters.

notes.quote: Pilots are generally arranged for in advance through ships’ agents and board incoming vessels from the pilot boat in the pilot boarding area off Cape Henlopen.
The pilot station and pilot boats may be contacted on VHF-FM channels 14 and 16.
The pilots carry portable radiotelephones for bridge-to-bridge communications on VHF-FM channel 13.
The Pilots’ Association for the Bay and River Delaware also provides qualified offshore “advisors” for the deepest draft vessels between Lighted Buoy “D” and the anchorage areas in Delaware Bay.
A notice of 24 hours before estimated arrival is requested for this service.
Pilots meet vessels at the pilot boarding area off Cape Henlopen using Delaware Bay Launch Service, which monitors VHF-FM channels 16 and 9.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage through the canal from Delaware River to Chesapeake City is provided by the Pilots’ Association for the Delaware Bay and River. (See Pilotage, Bay and River Delaware, indexed as such, chapter 6.) Pilotage from Chesapeake City to Maryland ports and to Washington, D.C., is provided by the Association of Maryland Pilots.

notes.quote: They board vessels at any Delaware River or Upper Chesapeake Bay port, the pilot boarding area off Cape Henlopen as described in chapter 6, or at the Reedy Point Anchorage near the east end of the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal.
Delaware Bay and River pilots use VHF-FM channel 14, and the Maryland pilots use VHF–FM channel 11; all associations use VHF-FM channel 13.
The traffic dispatcher at Chesapeake City also monitors VHF–FM channel 16 and channel 13 on a 24- hour basis.

items.head: Traffic Separation Schemes
items.quote: Traffic Separation Schemes for the Chesapeake Bay entrance have been established to aid navigation and to prevent collisions. The schemes are not intended in any way to supersede or alter the applicable Navigation Rules (See 33 CFR 167.1 through 167.15 and 167.200 through 167.203 , chapter 2, for limits and regulations and Traffic Separation Schemes, chapter 1, for additional information.)

items.quote: Pilotage on the York River is compulsory for all foreign vessels and for U.S. vessels under register in the foreign trade. Pilotage is optional for U.S. vessels in the coastwise trade that have on board a pilot licensed by the Federal Government to operate in these waters.

items.head: Harbor regulations
items.quote: Harbor regulations provide a speed limit of 10 mph when passing the wharf area of Alexandria, except in emergencies.

items.head: Harbor regulations
items.quote: The person in charge of any vessel 26 feet or more long entering the harbor, shall, if he intends to remain over 24 hours, report the date and time of arrival without delay and shall also report immediately before finally departing to the harbormaster at the Harbor Precinct wharf, Maine Avenue and M Street, SW. or to any police officer under his command.

items.head: Harbor Regulations
items.quote: A speed limit of 6 mph is enforced.
